method: codex --search (ChatGPT subscription), 2025-2026 official sources first; reviewed by the builder

cards: Foreign Visa and Mastercard work widely in shops, restaurants, convenience stores and taxis.
Amex and UnionPay work at many larger merchants. Confirm acceptance at small restaurants and independent shops.
Most stores have no card minimum. Carry a physical card because phone payments are less consistent.
cash: Keep cash for traditional markets, street food, small rural businesses and transit top-ups.
Suggested daily reserve: KRW50,000–100,000 for food and market purchases. Keep KRW1,000, KRW5,000 and KRW10,000 notes.
qr_wallets: Existing Alipay, WeChat Pay and UnionPay QR users can pay participating ZeroPay merchants. Check the displayed wallet logos.
September 2025: Japanese PayPay users gained Korean payments. Complete identity checks in Japan before departure.
transit: Buy Tmoney at convenience stores or participating subway stations. Carry cash for physical-card top-ups.
Compatible Galaxy phones can use Korea Tour Card with foreign-card reloads. Check device support before relying on it.
Convenience stores refund small Tmoney balances, subject to limits. Refunds above KRW50,000 require Tmoney Town near Seoul Station.
atm: Use Hana, Shinhan or KB machines marked Global ATM or overseas cards. Ordinary domestic machines may reject foreign cards.
Typical operator fees are KRW3,000–4,000, plus issuer charges. Choose KRW and cover your PIN.
korea.tipping: Tipping is not expected in restaurants, hotels or taxis.

cards: Foreign Visa and Mastercard work widely at hotels, chains and larger restaurants. Amex also works at many larger businesses.
Check UnionPay acceptance before ordering. Many urban taxis accept cards; small restaurants and rural businesses may require cash.
March 2025: PIN bypass generally ended. Know your card PIN; signing may not replace it when requested.
cash: Carry yen for markets, small restaurants, shrines, lockers and rural transport. Keep JPY1,000 notes and coins.
Suggested daily cash reserve: JPY5,000–10,000 for casual meals, markets and small purchases; carry more for shopping.
qr_wallets: Existing supported wallets, including Alipay and GCash, can scan participating PayPay merchant codes. Use your home wallet.
June 2026: PayPay expanded support to 35 overseas payment services. Check your wallet's Japan support before departure.
transit: Buy physical Welcome Suica at designated JR East airport machines. Reload the physical card with cash.
March 2025: Welcome Suica Mobile launched for compatible iPhones and Apple Watches, with Apple Pay card reloads.
Welcome Suica balances are non-refundable. Physical cards expire after 28 days; Welcome Suica Mobile expires after 180 days.
atm: Seven Bank machines inside 7-Eleven accept major foreign networks, including Amex and UnionPay. Japan Post is another reliable option.
Japan Post charges JPY220; Seven Bank fees depend on the card. Choose yen, cover your PIN and check issuer fees.
japan.tipping: Tipping is not customary. Pay the bill, including any stated service or table charge.

cards: Foreign Visa, Mastercard and UnionPay work at hotels, malls and larger restaurants. Confirm Amex acceptance before relying on it.
Street stalls, markets, tuk-tuks and most meter taxis need cash. Ride-hailing apps can charge a registered foreign card.
Some smaller merchants add card surcharges. Ask first, and choose THB when terminals offer currency conversion.
cash: Carry baht for street food, markets, local transport and taxi tolls. Drivers may struggle to change THB1,000.
Suggested daily reserve: THB500–1,000 for street meals and modest market purchases. Keep THB20, THB50 and THB100 notes.
qr_wallets: May 2025: TAGTHAi Easy Pay offers tourist QR payments through KBank PAY&TOUR. Register with your passport at participating exchange booths.
Fund PAY&TOUR with cash exchanged at KBank, then link it in TAGTHAi. Do not assume foreign-card top-ups work.
Supported home banking apps can pay participating Thai merchant QR codes through cross-border links. Ordinary personal PromptPay codes may fail.
transit: For Bangkok BTS, buy Rabbit at station offices with your passport; reload with cash. Rabbit excludes MRT Blue and Purple.
MRT Blue and Purple accept contactless Visa, Mastercard and UnionPay. November 2025: Airport Rail Link added bank-card payments.
Rabbit requires a physical card. Its purchase fee is non-refundable; ask a BTS office to refund eligible remaining value.
atm: Krungsri and SCB accept foreign cards. March 2026: Krungsri charges THB350 for Mastercard; Visa and UnionPay cost THB250.
Your issuer may charge extra. Use bank or mall machines, cover your PIN and decline conversion to your home currency.
thailand.tipping: Tipping is optional; rounding taxi fares is common. Check restaurant bills for an included service charge.

cards: Foreign Visa and Mastercard work at hotels, malls, supermarkets and larger restaurants. Amex acceptance is patchy.
Confirm UnionPay acceptance directly. Carry cash for street food, markets and meter taxis; Grab can charge a linked card.
Some hotels, boutiques and restaurants add roughly 3% for cards. Ask before paying and choose VND.
cash: Suggested daily reserve: VND500,000–1,000,000 for street meals, local transport and modest market purchases.
Keep VND10,000, VND20,000 and VND50,000 notes. Small vendors may lack change for VND500,000.
qr_wallets: April 2026: Chinese visitors gained Alipay payments at participating VIETQRGlobal merchants through the NAPAS connection.
Use an eligible Chinese Alipay account and participating merchant QR codes. Do not assume every personal VietQR code works.
transit: Ho Chi Minh City Metro Line 1 accepts Mastercard directly. Cash tickets remain an alternative at stations.
April 2025: equipped Ho Chi Minh City buses added foreign Visa and Mastercard payments, including Apple Pay and Samsung Pay.
Direct bank-card payments need no local balance to reload or refund. Keep cash for other buses and transport systems.
atm: VPBank and Vietcombank accept foreign cards. April 2026 reports show VPBank fee-free and Vietcombank around VND50,000; check the screen.
Issuer fees can apply. Choose VND, use machines inside banks or malls, and inspect the card slot.
vietnam.tipping: Tipping is optional in everyday restaurants and taxis; guides and personal service staff more commonly receive tips.

cards: Foreign Visa and Mastercard work at hotels, malls, chains and larger restaurants. Amex is less consistent; UnionPay is common.
Night markets, traditional markets and small restaurants often require cash. Confirm foreign-card acceptance before ordering.
Do not assume a taxi accepts your card. Use cash or book through an app with your card linked.
cash: Suggested daily reserve: TWD1,000 for street meals, snacks and local transport; carry more for market shopping.
Keep TWD100 notes and coins. Break TWD1,000 notes at larger shops before visiting markets.
qr_wallets: April 2026: Japanese PayPay users gained payments at participating TWQR merchants, including some night-market stalls.
Complete PayPay identity checks in Japan before departure. PayPay cannot pay MRT or bus fares, even beside TWQR logos.
transit: Buy EasyCard at MRT stations, airports or convenience stores; reload with cash at station machines or shop counters.
EasyCard cannot be added to Apple Wallet. Physical cards avoid restrictions affecting mobile versions and foreign phones.
Request balance refunds at Taipei Metro counters. The TWD100 card cost stays non-refundable; short visits usually incur TWD20 processing.
atm: Cathay United and Taiwan Cooperative machines accept foreign cards and often have no operator fee; CTBC commonly charges TWD100–150.
Fees depend on your card and machine. Choose TWD, inspect the slot and cover your PIN.
taiwan.tipping: Tipping is not expected. Restaurants may add a 10% service charge; an extra tip is unnecessary.

cards: Foreign Visa and Mastercard work widely in shops and restaurants. Check Amex and UnionPay acceptance at individual merchants.
Many taxis accept cards, sometimes with surcharges. Confirm with the driver before departure.
Some hawker stalls accept only cash or supported QR wallets. A card terminal elsewhere does not guarantee stall acceptance.
cash: Keep cash for hawker stalls, small purchases and taxi backup. Small notes prevent problems with change.
Suggested daily reserve: SGD30–50 for hawker meals and modest market purchases. Keep SGD2, SGD5 and SGD10 notes.
qr_wallets: Supported Alipay+ home wallets can pay participating merchants, including some hawker stalls. February 2026: coverage included 25 overseas apps.
Use your existing eligible home wallet and check its logo on SGQR. A PayNow-only code does not guarantee tourist access.
transit: Tap foreign Visa or Mastercard, including supported phone wallets, on buses and MRT. Foreign cards incur SGD0.60 per day.
May 2025: foreign Amex cards and supported wallets gained transit access without that administration fee. Use the same card or device throughout.
Alternatively, buy EZ-Link at station service points and reload with cash. Ticket offices refund eligible remaining value.
atm: DBS/POSB, UOB and OCBC accept foreign cards. Operator fees vary from zero to about SGD8; issuer fees may apply.
Check the displayed fee, choose SGD and cover your PIN. Use a bank-attached machine when possible.
singapore.tipping: Tipping is not expected; restaurants and hotels often include a service charge.
